newsitem.title: UK: UK Gay Pride Parade shows power of "pink pound".
newsitem.headline: UK Gay Pride Parade shows power of "pink pound".

text.p: When London's annual Gay Pride Parade fills the streets this Saturday, the array of drag queens and muscle-bound, leather-clad men will not be the only ones vying for the attention of the parade's expected 300,000 participants.
Marching in step with the outrageously costumed drag queens and exotic floats will be a host of corporate sponsors which are increasingly recognising the value of the so-called "pink pound."

"The main sponsor of Pride '97 is United Airlines, and we have also got support from Beefeater Gin, Finlander Vodka and Holsten Pils among others," a spokeswoman for the Pride Trust, the parade organiser, told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.

The Pride sponsors are leading a pack of companies that are beginning to specifically target the gay community as they recognise its huge spending power. The so-called "pink pound" is worth six billion pounds ($10 billion) a year in the UK alone, according to the Henley Centre for Forecasting, a market research firm.

"In the past few companies wanted to be openly associated with the gay market, but it's becoming much more usual for big companies to target gay consumers," said Liz Mackenzie, of Centaur Conferences, which recently organised a conference entitled "Marketing to the Pink Economy. "Not only do they have large disposable incomes but they also set trends," she said of the appeal of the gay community.

A spokesman for United Airlines said the company had decided to sponsor Pride '97 because, "We are a global business and the gay community has a propensity to travel quite extensively. It therefore seemed appropriate."

In the U.S and Australia marketing to gay people is well established. A survey published earlier this year in the U.S. by Simmons Market Research Bureau found that 28 percent of gays claimed to have a household income above $50,000 a year and that 89 percent of those surveyed will go out of their way to buy products that advertise to gay consumers.

In Britain, Virgin Group is running "gay shopping nights" at its Virgin Megastore on London's Oxford Street, British Airways Plc is organising gay package holidays, and insurance company Frizzell is running ads for its products in the gay press.
Europe's first gay department store, featuring branded clothing such as Levi and Diesel, a travel agency department and coffee shop, is due to open shortly in London's trendy Soho district.
The Pride Trust estimates that about one-fifth of the participants in Pride are not gay but are there to enjoy the spectacle.
The Parade will march through some of London's premier tourist areas including Piccadilly Circus and Trafalgar Square before ending up at Clapham Common for a night of dancing and entertainment.
